raw_response:
I will still put most of my land into cotton, because that is what I know best and what I have been doing. On 72 mu with only 2 people at home, I do not want too many scattered crops, so I will keep cotton as the main one and leave a smaller piece for sunflower. I usually start from what worked last year, then adjust a little. With well irrigation, I dare to spend a bit more on fertilizer because if the crop dries or stays weak, the loss is bigger than wasting some fertilizer. I only finished primary school, so I do not make it too complicated. I look at my own field, what neighbors did, and what the input seller says when it matches what I already saw. For cotton, I will use better seed than old saved seed, put enough base fertilizer, and then chase fertilizer in stages so the plants do not run out in the middle. Cotton takes more work and more spraying, but on good irrigated land it still brings money. For sunflower, I will keep it simpler, use hybrid seed, not push too much nitrogen, and keep the field clean so it stands straight and fills seed well. On a big area like mine, I do things a bit more steadily and I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than watch yield fall.
